correctness.rationale: Tracing the downdate gives g_i=||Ae_i||²/d_i, the Rayleigh quotient of A at A^{1/2}e_i. Thus Δ₀≤λ_max and Δ₁=tr(A²)/tr(A). Scaling λ_max to one and writing s for the other positive eigenvalues' sum yields (1+s)/(1+s²/(r−1)), maximized at s=√r−1. Rank one ties identically. The block family J_N/N ⊕ I_{r−1}/(√r+1) has gains 1 on the N-block and 1/(√r+1) on singletons, yielding the asserted limit. In size two the difference is (a−b)(g₁−g₂)/(2(a+b))=(a−b)²(1−|c|²/(ab))/(2(a+b))≥0; in size three J₂/2 ⊕ [2/3] gives 8/9 versus 13/15. For fixed real β>1, B_T has gains T on the m_T-block and one on the singleton; total block weight h_T=T^β m_T^{1−β} satisfies Th_T→0 under the stated q, so the ratio is asymptotic to T. These checks establish one-pivot expectations, not multistep performance. The supplied finite-test script was inspected, not run.

evidence: The earlier Frobenius proof takes t=m^a with 2/β<a<1/2 for β>4. The β=1 trace identity is an antecedent of the present bound.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For β>4 the earlier choice also yields trace-ratio divergence: trace expectation at β is at most t+m^{2−aβ}, whereas the uniform trace gain is asymptotic to m; indeed the β trace gain is asymptotic to t. Thus this subrange and the construction should not be credited as independent. Extending trace divergence to all β>1 uses the larger range 2/(β+1)<a<1 and is not supplied by the Frobenius theorem. The β=1 identity plus the Rayleigh bound provides an upper-bound route, but does not realize the extremal spectral profile at arbitrary ranks via coordinate multiplicities, or show the finite-size reversal.

value.rationale: A sharp rank-only bound answers how much uniform sampling can outperform the standard Cholesky pivot rule on the actual expected trace progress, and the rank-two construction shows why that guarantee cannot be transferred to any heavier exponent. The first possible reversal in size three provides a compact diagnostic. The result does not depend on calling the family new or extrapolating to multiple pivots.
